fields.h1: Build a New Employee Form That Tracks Every Deadline
fields.hero_description: A new employee form gathers a hire's details and tax paperwork before day one. Describe your packet, and Emergent builds one link that collects it and tracks each due date.
fields.features_heading: What a New Hire Packet Should Handle
fields.features_subheading: A printed packet gets signed and filed. Emergent's version knows which forms each hire owes and when each one is due.
fields.feature_1:
One link for the whole packet

Sends each hire a single link holding the information sheet, the W-4, Section 1 of the I-9 and your policy acknowledgments, with a progress bar showing the hire what remains.
fields.feature_2:
Personal details typed once

Asks for each personal detail a single time, then reuses the answer wherever a later form in the packet needs it again. The W-4 and the state certificate both draw on one record.
fields.feature_3:
State forms picked by work location

Adds the right state withholding certificate after the hire names a work location: NC-4 for a Charlotte hire, DE 4 for San Diego. Nobody sees a form their state does not use.
fields.feature_4:
Due dates counted from the start date

Puts two clocks on every record: the I-9 document review HR owes after day one, and the report to the state directory. Anything close to its deadline turns red for HR.
fields.feature_5:
Signatures filed with a date

Captures the hire's signature on every form and policy acknowledgment with a timestamp, then files a signed copy against the employee record in a database your company owns.
fields.feature_6:
Onboarding code you keep

Exports the full codebase to GitHub on paid plans. An engineer can wire the employee record into your payroll provider or HRIS, or you describe the change and Emergent writes it.

fields.usecase_heading: Onboarding Paperwork by Team and State
fields.tab_content_1:
Section 1 signed from her phone at home

Bluebird Kitchen texts every line cook one link after they accept the offer. Rosa Diaz opens it the night before her first shift and finishes 3 of 4 items, Section 1 of the I-9 among them. HR sees the handbook acknowledgment still open. Her I-9 document check is due within 3 business days after she starts.
fields.tab_content_2:
Phoenix gets the A-4, Detroit gets the MI-W4

Lumen Analytics hires in two states. Its form opens by asking where the hire will work, and the packet changes with the answer. A Phoenix hire gets Arizona's A-4, which the state wants within 5 days of starting. A Detroit hire gets Michigan's MI-W4, due by the first day. HR never picks state paperwork by hand.
fields.tab_content_3:
IT gets a laptop request with the last signature

At Lumen Analytics, a finished packet is the trigger. When Marcus Bell signs his final form, Emergent opens a ticket for his laptop and logins in the IT queue. His manager, Grace Liu, gets a Slack direct message with his start date. Nobody has to ask HR whether the paperwork is done.
fields.tab_content_4:
Day 17 of 20 and still unreported

Federal law gives employers 20 days to report a hire to the state. Kestrel Home Care adds aides every week, and its HR coordinator works from one list of hires not yet reported, sorted by days since hire. Jamie Cole sits at day 17 of 20 and stays red until HR files the report and marks it done.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a New Employee Form
fields.howto_description: Start from the paper packet HR hands out today. The seven steps follow a hire from the accepted offer through the first week.
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Send the link with the offer
fields.howto_step_1_des: Pull the packet HR uses now and sort it. Federal forms come first: the W-4 and the I-9. Then add your state withholding certificate and the direct deposit authorization. Policies a hire must acknowledge in writing go last.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask for legal name, preferred name, home address, phone, personal email, date of birth, and Social Security number. Job title, department, manager and start date are fields HR completes, which keeps the hire's view to questions about themselves.
fields.howto_step_3_des: A hire may complete Section 1 of the I-9 any time after accepting the offer, and no later than the first day of work. Sending the packet link with the acceptance email lets them finish it at home instead of on a clipboard at orientation.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Ask where the hire will work before any tax form appears. Arizona uses the A-4, Michigan the MI-W4, North Carolina the NC-4, and California the DE 4. Show the federal W-4 to everyone and only the state form that applies.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Put both clocks on the record
fields.howto_step_5_des: Once the hire starts, HR has 3 business days to examine identity and work documents and complete Section 2. The state report is due within 20 days of hire, and earlier in some states. Store both due dates with the employee.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Collect a signature on each form and acknowledgment, record when it was signed, and attach a copy to the employee record. Send the W-4 and state certificate to whoever runs payroll, and keep I-9s in a separate HR file.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Let a finished packet start day one
fields.howto_step_7_des: Treat the last signature as the signal for everything that follows. IT orders equipment and creates accounts, the manager learns the start date, and the new hire arrives to a desk that is ready instead of a stack of paper.

claims_to_source: Employees complete Section 1 of Form I-9 no later than their first day of employment, after accepting the offer, and employers complete Section 2 within 3 business days of the first day
The IRS says to ask all new employees for a signed Form W-4 when they start work
Form W-2 is the wage and tax statement an employer files and gives to each employee after the year ends
Employers must report each new hire to the state where they work within 20 days of hire, and some states require it sooner
New Arizona employees complete Form A-4 to choose their state withholding percentage, within 5 days of employment
Michigan employees submit Form MI-W4 on or before the date employment begins, and without it the employer withholds with no exemptions
North Carolina employees complete Form NC-4, and without it the employer withholds as single with no allowances
California employees complete Form DE 4 for state withholding because the W-4 covers federal withholding only, and without it the employer uses single with zero allowances
